title: The priest is a person
hookLine: priests get tired and lonely too
tomorrow: how do you walk someone toward a sacrament you can barely explain?

cards: Sunday night. The last Mass is over, the lot is empty, the lights in the church go off. Somewhere a priest might be eating leftovers alone, or answering one more call.
Mark's Gospel has a night like that. The apostles come back from their first mission full of stories, and the crowds won't stop.
Jesus says to them, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "Come apart into a desert place, and rest a little." Mark adds why: they hadn't even had time to eat.

teach.b: Jesus noticed his helpers were worn out.
The letter to the Hebrews says every priest is taken from among men, and that he can have compassion on those who stumble "because he himself also is compassed with infirmity."

Weakness wraps around him too, and that's part of why he can understand. You can smell it in the ordination rite. The bishop anoints the new priest's palms with chrism, olive oil mixed with sweet balsam.
Those are a person's hands: they get cold, they shake, they get tired. One to tell a friend: at the start of Mass the priest doesn't stand apart from the confession of sin.
He says the I confess with everyone, through my fault, and asks the people to pray for him. Catholics believe the sacraments act through Christ, not through the priest's own strength.
So the man can be tired and the Mass still be the Mass. And he can still use a thank you, a meal, and someone who prays for him by name.

how: At the start of Mass, priest and people confess together, and at the end of the I confess the people are asked to pray for one another; Catholics also pray for priests by name and for vocations.

games.q: what does “the priest is a person” mean?
o: a priest stops having needs once he's ordained
a priest stays human: tired, weak, needing prayer
a priest is a manager who runs the parish office

games.q: the priest is a person — tap the pairs.
p: olive oil and balsam for anointing
said by priest and people together
come apart and rest a little

s: at ordination, the bishop anoints the new priest's hands with chrism
olive oil and balsam, on a person's palms.
the priest skips the I confess at the start of Mass
he says it with everyone: through my fault.
in Mark 6, Jesus tells the worn-out apostles to keep going
he says come apart and rest a little; they hadn't even had time to eat.

games.q: your priest mixes up your grandmother's name at the Mass for her anniversary. your aunt is annoyed. what fits Hebrews 5?
o: remember he's human, tell him kindly, and pray for him.
write to the bishop; a priest shouldn't make mistakes.
say nothing, and avoid his Masses from now on.
games.why: Hebrews says the priest is compassed with infirmity himself, which is why he can have compassion. the same grace can run back to him.

practice: Look at your own hands, palms up. If you have a little olive oil or lotion nearby, rub a drop into them and notice the smell and the warmth.
Then bring to mind one priest you know or have seen, and his hands that have blessed and baptized and buried. If you pray, you can pray for him by name; if not, simply wish him rest.

wordCard.voice: The priest is a person. A man taken from among people and anointed for service, still human, still tired, still in need of prayer. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: weakness. Hebrews 5:2 says the priest himself is wrapped in it.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: pray for him, by name, the man inside the vestments. Go in peace.
